fields.title: Breaking Things on Purpose
fields.keyTakeaway: A Plan B that has not been tested does not work, and regular drills yield more measurable reliability than any investments in redundancy.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: We have Plan Bs, degradation modes, feature flags. How do we know they work?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: An untested backup path does not work — this is a rule, not pessimism. Every case of testing Plan B reviewed in this course found it broken: search kill switch, zone switchover, delivery service reconciliation, backup restore. Four out of four.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: [[chaos-engineering|Chaos engineering]] sounds radical, but in practice starts simply: **disable a component and see what happens.**
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: *Level 1.* Testing switches in a staging environment. Once a quarter, one hour of work. *Level 2.* Disabling an optional component in the live system during off-peak hours. Once a month. *Level 3.* [[game-day|Game days]] with a declared scenario: the team knows the date, but not what exactly will fail. *Level 4.* Automated random failures in production.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: Most products only need the first two, and they yield the bulk of the benefits.

fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: The fifth point is non-obvious and important: message templates, roles, channels — all this is also Plan B, and it also does not work without testing.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: The PM's role: **decide what to test and evaluate the result in product terms.** Not "the switch worked", but "the user saw popular items instead of recommendations, load time did not change, zero support tickets."
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Drills once a month, an hour on Wednesday morning.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/rows/0/1: Did not work — blank screen instead of catalog
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/rows/2/1: Cash on delivery worked, but the error message text was confusing
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/rows/3/1: 4 hours 20 minutes instead of the claimed hour
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/rows/4/1: Three issues: caches, webhooks, queue handler
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/rows/5/1: Templates found in 8 minutes, roles mixed up
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Four out of six found problems. After half a year of regular drills, the failure rate dropped to one in six, and this is the best measurable result of reliability work over the entire period.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: Side effect: the team stopped fearing failures. An incident turned from an event into a procedure.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Drills in production require maturity: clear degradation, fast rollback, readiness to explain. You must start with a staging environment and optional components, not the orders database.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: A Plan B that has not been tested does not work, and regular drills yield more measurable reliability than any investments in redundancy.
